meta.description: Keyword-driven Q&A config for the portfolio chat widget at anbu-aiportfolio.vercel.app. Not a generative model — match user input against 'patterns' per intent (case-insensitive, substring/keyword match) and return the matching 'response'. Falls back to 'fallback' intent if nothing matches. Patterns are intentionally broad (typos, casual phrasing, synonyms) to cover edge cases. Responses never contain raw URLs or contact details — always direct the user to 'the contact page' in words; the chat UI itself should render that phrase as a clickable link to /contact.

session.questionCounterNote: Increment counter on every USER message whose intent has countsTowardLimit = true. Persist counter client-side (e.g. localStorage) per browser session.
session.limitReachedResponse: You've hit the free question limit for this chat 🙂 For anything deeper — pricing, timelines, or your specific project — reach out to him through the contact page and he'll pick it up personally.

moderation.description: Basic profanity/inappropriate-language filter. Check user input against 'blockedTerms' (case-insensitive, word-boundary match) BEFORE running intent matching. If matched, return moderationResponse and do NOT count it toward the 3-question limit.
moderation.moderationResponse: Let's keep this respectful 🙂 I'm just a simple assistant here to answer questions about Anbu's work. Try asking about his skills, projects, or how he works with clients.

fallback.description: Used when no intent pattern matches and the message isn't profanity — covers off-topic questions, small talk unrelated to the portfolio, or anything the bot has no verified data on. Never invent or guess an answer.
fallback.response: I don't have a verified answer for that one — I only know what's on Anbu's portfolio (skills, projects, clients, philosophy, how he works). For anything specific or outside that, reach out to him through the contact page and Anbu will answer directly.

steps: 1. Lowercase and trim the user's message.
2. Check against moderation.blockedTerms first (word-boundary match). If matched, return moderationResponse immediately — don't touch the question counter.
3. If session question count >= session.maxQuestionsPerUser, return session.limitReachedResponse and stop.
4. Loop through 'intents' in array order; for each, check if any of its 'patterns' appears as a substring in the message. Return the first match's 'response'.
5. If an intent matched and its countsTowardLimit is true, increment the question counter.
6. If nothing matched, return fallback.response (does not count toward the limit, so users aren't penalized for phrasing the bot doesn't understand).

7. Never expose raw URLs or contact details (email/phone) in bot response text — always say 'reach out to him through the contact page' in words, and let the chat UI render that phrase as a clickable link to /contact rather than printing the URL.
